rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact street building with a clear U-like carved void and a single dominant mass. In all four views the same rule is legible, so it is not fragmented and it survives the multi-view coherence gate. The parcel containment and access response also appear coherent: the mass sits within the green boundary and the blue access edge is answered by an open seam/void rather than a sealed wall. The main weakness is that the silhouette is still somewhat box-derived and only moderately articulated in section; the opening is useful, but the upper mass does not yet fully register as a distinctive public threshold or terrace section. Program-wise it plausibly supports neighborhood living / mixed-use because it preserves an active ground relation and an occupiable void, and it avoids large-span or tower typologies. It resonates most with references that use courtyard subtraction, low-rise spread, and bridge/cut massing, though it is less site-responsive and less sectional than the strongest precedents.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more sculptural and pavilion-like than the candidate; do not copy the curved roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise massing with a large carved central void and a bridge-like upper connector can support a neighborhood/public program while keeping the ground legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger campus/higher-density composition than the candidate; tower-like elements are not transferable here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard-based campus composition and stepped/terraced low-rise parts can organize a public neighborhood program around open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more civic and urban-plaza oriented; avoid over-reading transparency as a required condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A rectilinear mass with a major cutout and overhanging upper volume can create an active public threshold at the ground.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more compact and box-like; the greenhouse/roof appendage language is not directly transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise form with a central void and gently folded roof logic gives a strong neighborhood-scale public interior/exterior relation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more complex and site-responsive, with stronger winging and bridging than the current candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Spread-out composition, courtyard, and connected wings with terrace-like section moves are well aligned to neighborhood living and public threshold needs.
